examples.en: My wallet is in my pants pocket.
I took my keys out of my pocket.
The coat pockets are deep, so my hands stay warm.
The pocket is so small that my phone doesn't fit.
The child filled his pocket with candy.
Walking with your hands in your pockets is dangerous.

explain: 옷에 달린 주머니도, 작은 물건을 넣는 작은 자루도 모두 '주머니'예요. '주머니에 넣다', '주머니에서 꺼내다'처럼 '에', '에서'와 함께 써요. '주머니 사정'처럼 돈 이야기에도 써요.

phrases.example: 이번 달은 주머니 사정이 안 좋아서 여행은 못 가요.
phrases.en: My finances are tight this month, so I can't go on a trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가지고 있는 돈의 형편을 말해요. '주머니가 가볍다'도 돈이 별로 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes how much money you have on hand. '주머니가 가볍다' also means you have little money.

explain_en: Both a pocket sewn into clothes and a small pouch for carrying things are '주머니'. It goes with '에' and '에서', as in '주머니에 넣다' and '주머니에서 꺼내다'. It also appears in money talk, as in '주머니 사정'.

examples.ko: 밀가루 백오십 그램에 물을 넣고 섞어요.
examples.en: Add water to 150 grams of flour and mix.
Kyunghee kneads the flour dough with practiced hands.
I bought flour and sugar to make bread.
My stomach feels uncomfortable when I eat flour-based foods.
The batter for pancakes is made with flour.
Please buy wheat flour, not rice flour.

explain: '밀'은 곡식이고 '밀가루'는 그것을 갈아 만든 가루예요. '쌀가루'는 쌀로 만든 가루라서 떡을 만들 때 많이 써요. '밀가루 음식'은 면, 빵, 부침개처럼 밀가루로 만든 음식을 묶어서 말해요.

phrases.en: I like flour-based foods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 면이나 빵처럼 밀가루로 만든 음식을 묶어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group term for foods made of flour, like noodles and bread.

phrases.en: I make flour dough.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in cooking.

phrases.en: I bought a bag of flour at the mart.
phrases.nuance_en: How to count flour.

explain_en: '밀' is the grain and '밀가루' is the powder ground from it. '쌀가루' is rice flour, often used for rice cakes. '밀가루 음식' groups together foods made with wheat flour, like noodles, bread and pancakes.

examples.en: I put on black socks.
My favorite color is black.
I bought new black shoes.
I want to dye my hair black.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 검정과 흰색 두 가지가 있어요.
examples.en: This bag comes in two colors, black and white.
Today I wore all black, top to bottom.

explain: '검정'은 명사라서 '검정 양말'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 바로 쓸 수 있어요. 형용사 '검다'는 '검은 양말'처럼 모양이 바뀌어요. '검은색', '까만색'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I bought a black bag.
phrases.nuance_en: Widely used with the same meaning as '검정'.

phrases.en: I like black shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검은색'과 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '검은색', and it sounds more casual in speech.

phrases.en: I'm wearing black clothes today.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective '검다' changes to '검은' before a noun.

explain_en: '검정' is a noun, so it can go directly before another noun, as in '검정 양말'. The adjective '검다' changes its form: '검은 양말'. '검은색' and '까만색' are also commonly used.

dis.h: short noun form without color suffix
gh: standard everyday word for black color

p.n: 까만색 feels like a deeper, pitch black.

examples.en: I cut the paper with scissors.
Could you lend me your scissors?
Where are the scissors?
Please put the scissors back in place after you use them.
These scissors are too big.
At the salon they cut my hair with scissors.

explain: 영어 scissors와 달리 한 개로 세요. '가위 하나', '가위 두 개'처럼 말해요. 도구로 쓸 때는 '가위로 자르다'처럼 '로'와 함께 쓰고, 가위질하는 것은 '가위질'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I cut hair with scissors.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '로' to name the tool.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is good at cutting with scissors.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the act of cutting with scissors.

phrases.example: 책상 위에 가위 두 개가 있어요.
phrases.en: There are two pairs of scissors on the desk.
phrases.nuance_en: Scissors are counted with '개'.

explain_en: Unlike English 'scissors', it is counted as one item: '가위 하나', '가위 두 개'. As a tool it goes with '로' (가위로 자르다), and the act of cutting with scissors is called '가위질'.

examples.en: I laid small stones in the garden.

examples.ko: 겨울에 너무 추워서 정원의 나무가 죽었어요.
examples.en: It was so cold in winter that the trees in the garden died.

examples.ko: 우리 집 정원에는 장미가 많이 피었어요.
examples.en: Lots of roses have bloomed in our garden.
Tending a garden is my hobby.
We had a barbecue in the garden on the weekend.
I want to live in a house with a big garden.

explain: '정원'은 꽃과 나무를 보기 좋게 꾸민 곳이고 '마당'은 집 앞뒤의 빈 땅이에요. 정원은 '가꾸다'와 잘 어울려요. '정원 초과'의 '정원'(定員)은 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: My grandmother tends the garden every morning.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that goes best with 'jeongwon'.

phrases.en: Our school has a large garden.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the size of a garden.

phrases.en: All the flowers in the garden bloomed beautifully.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '의' to talk about things in the garden.

explain_en: '정원' is a place decorated with flowers and trees, while '마당' is the open yard around a house. It pairs well with '가꾸다' (to tend). The '정원' (定員, capacity) in '정원 초과' is a different word that just sounds the same.

examples.en: I like Korean cooking.
My husband is a good cook.

examples.ko: 저녁에 요리를 할 거예요. 뭐 먹고 싶어요?
examples.en: I'm going to cook this evening. What do you want to eat?
What is today's special dish?

examples.ko: 일요일에는 형이 요리를 하고 제가 청소를 해요.
examples.en: On Sundays my older brother cooks and I clean.

explain: ‘음식’은 먹는 것 전체예요. ‘요리’는 만드는 일이나 만든 음식이에요. ‘중국 요리’, ‘한국 요리’처럼 나라 이름과 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 상대 팀을 마음대로 요리했어요.
phrases.en: to handle or toy with (an opponent or a problem) skillfully
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 아니라 사람이나 일을 솜씨 있게 마음대로 다룰 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: not about food; used when you handle a person or a task skillfully and as you please
phrases.en_equiv: to handle or toy with (an opponent or a problem) skillfully

dict_examples.ko: 이 양념장은 한번 만들어 놓으면 다양한 요리에 활용할 수 있다.
dict_examples.en: Once you make this seasoning sauce, you can use it in all kinds of dishes.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 바다 냄새가 그대로 풍기는 신선한 요리에 구미가 당겼다.
dict_examples.en: The fresh dish, still smelling of the sea, whetted my appetite.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: ‘음식’ is food in general. ‘요리’ is the act of cooking or a dish you made. It goes with country names, as in ‘중국 요리’ and ‘한국 요리’.

examples.en: There are many ski resorts in Gangwon Province.
In January, the ski resort is crowded.
I go to the ski resort with friends on weekends.
Ski resorts close when the snow melts.
This ski resort has a wide beginner course.
You can rent equipment at the ski resort.

explain: '스키'에 장소를 뜻하는 '-장'이 붙은 말이에요. '수영장', '운동장'도 같은 방식이에요. 가는 곳이라서 '스키장에 가다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: This winter I'm going to a ski resort with a friend.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a destination, so it takes '에'.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a ski resort

phrases.en: I played at the ski resort all day on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스키장에서 하는 일을 말할 때는 '에서'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에서' for what you do at the resort.
phrases.en_equiv: to have fun at a ski resort

phrases.en: There are many restaurants near the ski resort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스키장 주변의 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about places around the ski resort.

explain_en: It is '스키' plus '-장', which marks a place, like '수영장' and '운동장'. Since it is a destination, it goes with '에', as in '스키장에 가다'.

usage: 대학 = college/university. In daily speech 대학교 is more common for the place.

examples.en: I'm starting college next year.
I met a friend from my college days.
I study Korean at college.
My younger sibling is a college freshman.
There are many restaurants in front of the college.

explain: “대학 일 학년”처럼 학년과 같이 말해요. 학교 이름에는 “대학교”가 붙어요: 서울대학교.

phrases.en: My older sister is a college student.
phrases.nuance_en: A student who attends college.

phrases.en: There is a university near my house.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 대학교 in the name of a school.

phrases.en: I attend a college in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you are currently a college student.

dict_examples.ko: 신입 사원은 대학에서 경영학을 전공했다고 한다.
dict_examples.en: They say the new employee majored in business administration in college.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: You say it together with the year, like “대학 일 학년” (first year of university). School names take “대학교”: 서울대학교.

dis.h: general word for college or university

p.n: 단대 names a faculty inside a university, so it does not work for 'going to college' in general.

examples.ko: 지갑을 안 가져와서 주인아저씨께 외상을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I didn't bring my wallet, so I asked the owner to let me pay later.
The owner gave us a free drink.
The owner of this shop is always kind.

examples.ko: 주인아저씨, 여기 물 좀 더 주세요.
examples.en: Sir, could we get some more water here?
I decided the moving date with the landlord.
I asked the stationery shop owner for directions.

explain: 동네 가게나 식당의 남자 주인을 친근하게 부르거나 말하는 표현이에요. 부를 때는 '사장님'이 더 정중하고 많이 써요. 여자 주인은 '주인아주머니'라고 하고, 집의 주인은 '집주인'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Boss, how much is this?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 주인을 부를 때 가장 정중하고 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most polite and common way to address a shop owner.

phrases.en: The owner gave me more side dishes.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to refer to a female owner.

phrases.en: I called the landlord.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 빌려주는 주인을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the owner of a house you rent.

explain_en: It is a friendly way to call or talk about a male owner of a neighborhood shop or restaurant. When addressing someone, '사장님' is more polite and very common. A female owner is '주인아주머니', and the owner of a house can also be called '집주인'.

t90.ax: The owner gave us a free drink.

examples.en: We eat dinner together as a family.
What shall we eat for dinner today?
Mom has set out dinner and is waiting.
I'll finish my homework before dinner.

examples.ko: 저녁밥이 다 식기 전에 어서 오세요.
examples.en: Come quickly before dinner gets cold.
I was busy and worked without even eating dinner.

explain: '저녁'만 말해도 저녁 식사를 뜻할 때가 많고, '저녁밥'은 밥이라는 음식을 조금 더 느끼게 하는 편한 말이에요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 '저녁 식사'가 어울려요. '아침밥, 점심밥, 저녁밥'을 세트로 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Did you eat dinner?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '밥'을 빼고 이렇게 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, people often drop '밥' and say it this way.

phrases.en: Dinner is at seven o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 격식 있는 자리나 안내하는 말에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in more formal situations or announcements.

phrases.en: My mom is cooking dinner.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing dinner yourself.

explain_en: Just saying '저녁' can already mean the evening meal, while '저녁밥' is a casual word that puts more focus on the meal itself. In formal settings, '저녁 식사' fits better. It helps to learn '아침밥, 점심밥, 저녁밥' as a set.
